prerequisites: Review of Algebra and Geometry topics
Review of Applications, Functions, and Graphs topics

learning_outcomes.text: Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, although supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge on: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.

syllabus_topics: TOOLS: Review of prior knowledge, introduction to MAXIMA, matricial algebra concepts (matrices, determinants, systems of linear equations).

VECTOR SPACES AND MATRICES: Fundamental structure of linear algebra (vector space), conditions for a subset to be a vector subspace, characterization, generation and size of subspaces, concepts of subspaces, sum of subspaces, dimension of a vector space and its main properties.

LINEAR APPLICATIONS: Linear applications, analytical representation using matrices, conservation of vector space structure, kernel and image of a linear application, matricial representation of a linear application, basis changes.
MATRIX DIAGONALIZATION: Spectral theory, calculation of eigenvalues and eigenvectors, iterative techniques of numerical linear algebra for finding eigenvalues and eigenvectors.

ORTHOGONALITY: Euclidean space, concept of scalar product, definition of orthogonality, distance, and angle, orthogonal matrices and their advantages, least squares problem and its application to non-linear models.

BILINEAR AND QUADRATIC FORMS: Importance of conics and quadrics in engineering problems, application of previous results to study their analytical expression and classification, characterization and classification of conics and quadrics.
teaching_methods: Autonomous work (study of theoretical content, problem-solving)
Interaction with teaching staff, tutors, and students
Completion of assessment activities (self-assessment, continuous assessment, face-to-face tests)
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as the sum of the face-to-face exam score plus the scores from PEC1 and PEC2, provided the face-to-face exam score is 4 or higher. If the face-to-face exam score is less than 4, the final grade is solely the face-to-face exam score. The face-to-face exam has a maximum score of 10 points. Each continuous assessment test (PEC) contributes a maximum of 0.5 points, for a total of 1 point if both are completed, provided the exam score is 4 or higher. No material is allowed during the exam; errors lead to penalties, with conceptual errors penalized more severely.
